title.narrative: Tonga Climate Finance Strategy and donor engagement support

description.narrative: The overall objective is to enable the Government of Tonga to access climate financing more effectively and efficiently to drive its net zero-emissions transition and build national resilience. This is achieved through three interconnected pathways. Firstly, by securing the endorsement and official adoption of the new Climate Finance Strategy. Secondly, by strengthening the communications and accessibility of the Tonga Climate Change Fund, leading to increased funding approvals. Finally, by ensuring the prioritization and strategic communication of the Tonga Energy Road Map Plus Investment Plan projects to potential investors and donors. The project targets ambitious outcomes, including at least $5 million of investments in the pipeline and at least $1 million approved through the Climate Change Fund by the project’s conclusion.

Tonga faces severe climate change impacts, including rising sea levels, changing rainfall patterns, and more intense tropical cyclones. These issues negatively affect the nation's development and the livelihoods of its citizens. Although the government invests significantly in climate mitigation and resilience using public finances, it requires substantial external support for financing, capacity building, and technology investments. Despite having various policy instruments in place, Tonga has struggled to secure the necessary climate financing to transition to a low-emissions economy, particularly for sustainable energy and transport, and to build stronger adaptation and resilience across all sectors. This project is designed to bridge this gap, ensuring the country can effectively attract and utilize global climate funds to secure its future.
